definition: Studierfenster or StudierFenster (SF) is a free, non-commercial open science client/server-based medical imaging processing online framework.
details: It offers capabilities, like viewing medical data (computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), etc.) in two- and three-dimensional space directly in the standard web browsers, like Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Safari, and Microsoft Edge. Other functionalities are the calculation of medical metrics (dice score and Hausdorff distance), manual slice-by-slice outlining of structures in medical images (segmentation), manual placing of (anatomical) landmarks in medical image data, viewing medical data in virtual reality, a facial reconstruction and registration of medical data for augmented reality, one click showcases for COVID-19 and veterinary scans, and a Radiomics module. Other features of Studierfenster are the automatic cranial implant design with a neural network, the inpainting of aortic dissections with a generative adversarial network, an automatic aortic landmark detection with deep learning in computed tomography angiography scans, and a GrowCut algorithm implementation for image segmentation. Studierfenster is currently hosted on a server at the Graz University of Technology in Austria, and expanded jointly with the Institute for Artificial Intelligence i

explainer.lead: Studierfenster is a free, non-commercial open science framework for processing medical images directly in a web browser. It matters because clinicians and researchers can view and analyse CT and MRI data without installing specialist software.

tiers.eli5: It is a website where you open medical scans and look at them in 2D or 3D, right in your browser, without installing anything.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to view scans and to do tasks like manual slice-by-slice segmentation, landmark placement and metric calculation such as the Dice score and Hausdorff distance. A pitfall is that outlining is manual, so results depend on the operator.
tiers.paperLevel: A client/server online framework built on standard web browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge), offering two- and three-dimensional viewing plus metrics including the Dice score and Hausdorff distance; it is free and non-commercial.

explainer.example: A researcher opens a CT volume in the browser, outlines a structure slice by slice, and the framework computes the Dice score against a reference segmentation.
